items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Pop Smith, a trumpet player who was a giant, was in this band.

ctx.x: Well, firstly, Fletcher Henderson wrote the most difficult music that I'd ever read. You know, as a matter of fact he would write in G flat. These were unheard of keys. And these guys were superb musicians. You know, G flat, B natural, A natural. He would write in all these keys, of Stealing Apples, some of the tunes, and of -- Benny Goodman used his whole library when he formed his band. He just took Fletcher's whole library, the things that we were doing at that time, and this made -- this really made Benny.

But this band, coming back to this band, these guys were so full of fun, they used to pull jokes on me. I was like a youngster in the band, and they would stage fake fights and I would go and try to separate them and we just had a marvelous time. But as I say these were real pros. Pop Smith, a trumpet player who was a giant, was in this band. Jonah Jones was in this band.
Was the trombone player Claude Jones?
